result.topic_en: Scholion 2 shows how a particular interpolating solution y = X can be generalised by adding an arbitrary function of a product vanishing at all the nodes; Problem 2 then applies the interpolation to sines of given arcs, letting the arc become infinitely small to obtain an identity among series that are each summable.

) 162 (
Scholion 2.
§. 6. Antequam autem huiusmodi casus euoluam, in genere obseruasse iuuabit, quod si pro quocunque casu oblato aequatio satisfaciens inter binas variabiles $x$ et $y$ fuerit inuenta, quam hoc modo designabo: $y = X$, ita vt sit $X = \alpha x + \beta x^3 + \gamma x^5 + \delta x^7 +$ etc. tum inde facile aequationem multo latius patentem et pariter satisfacientem formari posse. Statuatur enim:
$Q = x \cdot \frac{xx-aa}{aa} \cdot \frac{xx-bb}{bb} \cdot \frac{xx-cc}{cc} \cdot \frac{xx-dd}{dd}$, etc.
quae quantitas euanescit pro omnibus valoribus ipsius $x$ propositis:
$x = 0,\ x = \pm a,\ x = \pm b,\ x = \pm c$, etc.
idemque praestabunt omnes functiones ipsius $Q$, quae cum ipsa $Q$ euanescentes: ex quo manifestum est, si statuatur $y = X + Q$, vel $y = X + f:Q$, omnibus conditionibus aeque satisfieri. Quoniam igitur haec functio $f:Q$ omnino est arbitraria, dummodo euanescat facto $Q = 0$, haec aequatio: $y = X + f:Q$ solutionem generalissimam exhibere, est censenda.
Problema 2.
§. 7. Sint $a, b, c, d$, etc. quotcunque arcus circulares, existente radio $= 1$, valores autem $p, q, r, s$, etc. sint sinus eorundem arcuum, quandoquidem hoc casu ea proprietas locum habet, vt arcubus negatiuis iidem sinus negatiue sumti respondeant; hinc proxime definire rationem inter diametrum et peripheriam[?].
Solutio.
Cum hic sit $p = \sin. a$, $q = \sin. b$, $r = \sin. c$, etc. aequatio inter $x$ et $y$ ita erit comparata, vt sumto pro $x$

arcu circuli, quantitas $y$ proxime eius sinum sit expressura, fiatque $y = \sin. x$. Definitis ergo per praecedens problema coefficientibus $A, B, C, D$, etc. habebitur haec aequatio:
$\sin. x = Ax + Bx(xx-aa) + Cx(xx-aa)(xx-bb) +$ etc.
quae adeo veritati est consentanea, quoties fuerit vel
$x = 0$, vel $x = \pm a$, vel $x = \pm b$, vel $x = \pm c$ etc.
Statuamus nunc arcum $x$ infinite paruum, et quia tum eius sinus, $\sin. x$ ipsi arcui $x$ aequatur, oritur haec aequatio:
$1 = A - Baa + Caabb - Daabbcc + Eaabbccdd -$ etc.
Substituamus hic pro litteris $A, B, C, D$, etc. valores supra inuentos, ac perueniemus ad hanc aequationem:
$1 = \frac{p}{a}\left(1 - \frac{aa}{aa-bb} + \frac{aabb}{(aa-bb)(aa-cc)} - \frac{aabbcc}{(aa-bb)(aa-cc)(aa-dd)} + \text{etc.}\right)$
$- \frac{q}{b}\left(\frac{aa}{bb-aa} - \frac{aabb}{(bb-aa)(bb-cc)} + \frac{aabbcc}{(bb-aa)(bb-cc)(bb-dd)} - \text{etc.}\right)$
$+ \frac{r}{c}\left(\frac{aabb}{(cc-aa)(cc-bb)} - \frac{aabbcc}{(cc-aa)(cc-bb)(cc-dd)} + \text{etc.}\right)$
$- \frac{s}{d}\left(\frac{aabbcc}{(dd-aa)(dd-bb)(dd-cc)} - \text{etc.}\right)$
etc.
quae reducitur ad hanc, in qua omnes series sibi sunt similes:
$1 = \frac{p}{a}\left(1 + \frac{aa}{bb-aa} + \frac{aabb}{(bb-aa)(cc-aa)} + \frac{aabbcc}{(bb-aa)(cc-aa)(dd-aa)} + \text{etc.}\right)$
$- \frac{aaq}{b(bb-aa)}\left(1 + \frac{bb}{aa-bb} + \frac{bbcc}{(aa-bb)(cc-bb)} + \frac{bbccdd}{(aa-bb)(cc-bb)(dd-bb)} + \text{etc.}\right)$

$- \frac{aabbccs}{d(dd-aa)(dd-bb)(dd-cc)}\left(1 + \frac{dd}{aa-dd} + \text{etc.}\right)$
etc.

items.quote: si statuatur $y = X + Q$, vel $y = X + f:Q$, omnibus conditionibus aeque satisfieri
items.english: If one sets y = X + Q, or y = X + f:Q, all the conditions are equally satisfied.

items.quote: haec aequatio: $y = X + f:Q$ solutionem generalissimam exhibere, est censenda.
items.english: This equation y = X + f:Q is to be regarded as giving the most general solution.

items.quote: Sint $a, b, c, d$, etc. quotcunque arcus circulares, existente radio $= 1$, valores autem $p, q, r, s$, etc. sint sinus eorundem arcuum, quandoquidem hoc casu ea proprietas locum habet, vt arcubus negatiuis iidem sinus negatiue sumti respondeant; hinc proxime definire rationem inter diametrum et peripheriam[?].
items.english: Let a, b, c, d, etc. be any number of circular arcs, with radius = 1, and let the values p, q, r, s, etc. be the sines of these arcs, since in this case the property holds that the same sines taken negatively correspond to the negative arcs; from this, to determine approximately the ratio between the diameter and the circumference.

items.quote: Quaelibet autem harum serierum sponte est summabilis
items.english: Each of these series is, moreover, readily summable.
